attacks.claim: Guardians can receive hold-ready texts for juvenile cards, so a minor's holds are disclosed to a guardian account. The legal review (LGL-118) is described only as covering the privacy policy, and nothing addresses state library-confidentiality rules for minors or whether guardian linkage is verified.
attacks.evidence: 'guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account' / ABSENT: legal scope for minors' records and guardian authorization

attacks.claim: On permanent SMS withdrawal, consent records and numbers are deleted within 30 days. That removes proof of consent and the STOP suppression list, so opted-out numbers could be re-texted if SMS returns and the TCPA defense evidence is lost.
attacks.evidence: 'numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed'

attacks.claim: The spend-cap fallback sends automated phone calls to every opted-in patron. Those calls are not covered by the $900 SMS provider cap or the BM-26-14 budget, so the fallback can produce unbounded spend.
attacks.evidence: 'every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)' / ABSENT: call volume, cost, or cap for the fallback channel

attacks.claim: STOP is honored only if the signed webhook clears the opt-in flag. Monitoring alerts on signature failures but not on webhook lag or missing STOP events, so a stalled webhook could allow texts to continue after STOP, a TCPA exposure.
attacks.evidence: 'which clears the opt-in flag' / alert: 'webhook signature failures > 0' with no webhook-delivery or STOP-sync alert

attacks.claim: The public announcement says texts go to every cardholder, but the feature is opt-in and excludes juvenile cards. This misstates the program in an external communication.
attacks.evidence: 'Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder.'

attacks.claim: The QA ran against the provider in test mode with a $5 test cap, not the production $900 cap. Carrier filtering and spend-cap fallback were therefore not validated under production conditions, yet the QA table reports them as Pass.
attacks.evidence: 'against the production SMS provider account in test mode' and 'Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass'

attacks.claim: Accessibility claims for the locker kiosk (high-contrast mode, audio guidance, reach range) have no QA evidence. The QA table covers only the opt-in form with NVDA and VoiceOver, and the staff pilot was not tested for locker accessibility.
attacks.evidence: 'audio guidance through a headphone jack' / ABSENT: locker accessibility test results or reach measurement in QA summary

attacks.claim: Per-cell lockout after five wrong codes lets anyone who has passed card authentication lock out cells, disrupting pickups across a 48-cell bank until the 4-hour vendor SLA.
attacks.evidence: '5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff'

attacks.claim: The pickup code and locker location are sent in plaintext SMS, retained by the provider for 30 days and visible on lock screens. Pickup code exposure is a credential-like leak even though a card is also required.
attacks.evidence: 'Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14' / 'message logs 30 days'

attacks.claim: The IP address stored in the consent record has no stated retention period, which conflicts with the stated data-minimization approach.
attacks.evidence: 'consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version)' / ABSENT: retention for consent records

attacks.claim: Messages queued outside hours all release at 08:00, which can create a delivery spike. No throughput limit or staggering is specified for provider or 10DLC rate caps.
attacks.evidence: 'anything later is queued to 08:00' / ABSENT: throttling or rate limit

attacks.claim: When locker_pickup is turned off, outstanding locker codes already texted are not stated to be invalidated, so codes may remain usable against decommissioned cells.
attacks.evidence: 'holds ... remapped to the branch desk' / ABSENT: invalidation of outstanding locker codes

attacks.claim: Patron local time is used for quiet hours, but the source of timezone is not specified. The pickup deadline is date-only while codes expire at the deadline, so the exact expiry time is ambiguous.
attacks.evidence: 'Texts are sent only 08:00-20:00 patron local time' / 'pick up by Sat Nov 14'

attacks.claim: Single SMS provider with no documented alternate or exit path. Messaging and 10DLC registration are tied to one vendor.
attacks.evidence: 'the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA'

attacks.claim: No material display issue found beyond the copy concern already noted.
attacks.evidence: 'Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass'

attacks.claim: No material issue found; locker and SMS flows address pickup outside hours with a service-desk fallback.
attacks.evidence: 'Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours'

attacks.claim: Spanish message bodies are not shown or verified, only the opt-in flow. Spanish-speaking patrons may receive untested copy.
attacks.evidence: 'English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference' / ABSENT: Spanish message body and QA

attacks.claim: No material issue found; flags are defined in config and rollback has a tested remap script.
No additional gate-worthy issue found beyond the attacks above.
